Encoded values

Source: R/naxp_encoded.R
naxp_encoded.Rd

A naxp_encoded vector holds encoded values together with the naxp that encoded them, so it can always be decoded. naxp_encode() returns one, and naxp_encoded() makes one from bare values, such as values read from a database or a file.

Usage

naxp_encoded(values, naxp)

Arguments

values

An integer or double vector of whole numbers from 0 to the naxp's maximum encoded value. NA is an error.

naxp

A naxp from naxp_parse(), a pattern string or a naxp_encoded vector, whose naxp is used.

Value

A naxp_encoded vector the same length as values, with its names.

Details

The values are integers where the naxp's maximum encoded value is at most 2^31 - 1, and doubles where it is at most 2^53. Above 2^53 is an error. 0 stands for text that is not valid. Encoded values are never NA.

A naxp_encoded vector prints as the text it decodes to, with 0 shown as <invalid (0)>. as.character() gives the text, with NA for 0, and as.integer() or as.numeric() give the bare values.

Subsetting, rep(), rev(), unique() and sort() return naxp_encoded vectors with the same naxp, and split() returns a list of them. A naxp_encoded vector can be a data frame column. order() and match() return integer indices, and table() counts each distinct value, labelled with its text, excluding 0. Assigning into a naxp_encoded vector accepts another with the same naxp, or text, which is encoded. c() combines naxp_encoded vectors with the same naxp.

Encoded values are compared only for equality. == and != compare a naxp_encoded vector with one with the same naxp, with text, which is encoded first, or with numbers as bare values, so x == 0 finds the invalid text. Arithmetic, <, > and summaries such as max() raise errors. sort() and order() sort by encoded value.

Examples

nl_postcode <- naxp_parse(r"(\9\9\9\9 \s!! \A\A)")

codes <- naxp_encoded(c(684114, 0, 6760000), nl_postcode)
codes
#> <naxp_encoded[3]> \9\9\9\9 \s!! \A\A
#> [1] 1012 AB       <invalid (0)> 9999 ZZ      
codes == "1012 AB"
#> [1]  TRUE FALSE FALSE
codes == 0
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE FALSE

data.frame(postcode = codes)
#>        postcode
#> 1       1012 AB
#> 2 <invalid (0)>
#> 3       9999 ZZ
